questions.q: If two events $A$ and $B$ are statistically independent with $P(A) = 0.4$ and $P(B) = 0.3$, find the joint probability $P(A \cap B)$.
Are the events in question 2 statistically independent?
choices: Cannot be determined without conditional probabilities
questions.answer: Since $P(A \cap B) = 0.20 = P(A)P(B)$, the definition of independence is satisfied exactly.

sections.heading: Section 2: Conditional Probability and the Chain Rule

questions.q: Given $P(A) = 0.6$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0.18$, calculate the conditional probability $P(B|A)$.
In an autoregressive language model, write the joint probability of a sequence of three tokens $P(w_1, w_2, w_3)$ using the probability Chain Rule.
questions.answer: By exact probability decomposition: $P(w_1, w_2, w_3) = P(w_1) P(w_2|w_1) P(w_3|w_1, w_2)$.

questions.q: Factory line 1 produces $60\%$ of microchips with defect rate $2\%$. Line 2 produces $40\%$ with defect rate $5\%$. What is the total probability that a random chip is defective?
In question 7, if a selected chip is defective, what is the probability it came from Line 2?
State the Law of Total Probability for an exhaustive partition $\{A_1, A_2, \dots, A_k\}$ of the sample space.
questions.answer: Every element in $B$ belongs to exactly one partition $A_i$, giving $P(B) = \sum P(B \cap A_i) = \sum P(B|A_i)P(A_i)$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Bayes Theorem in Machine Learning and Screening

questions.q: In medical screening, a disease has prevalence $P(D) = 0.01$. The test has sensitivity $P(+|D) = 0.99$ and false positive rate $P(+|\neg D) = 0.02$. What is the posterior probability $P(D|+)$ that a positive patient has the disease?
What is the foundational simplifying assumption of the Naive Bayes text classifier?
choices: Features (words) are conditionally independent given the class label
questions.answer: Naive Bayes assumes $P(x_1, \dots, x_n | C) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(x_i | C)$, dramatically reducing parameter count.

questions.q: In Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation, how does the optimization objective differ from standard Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)?
choices: MAP incorporates a prior distribution: $\theta_{MAP} = \arg\max [\ln P(D|\theta) + \ln P(\theta)]$
MAP ignores all observed training data
MAP only applies to linear models
MAP minimizes variance instead of error
questions.answer: MAP maximizes posterior $\propto$ likelihood $\times$ prior, functioning mathematically like regularized MLE.
